reason: The hypothesis relies on L-PBF benefits demonstrated in CoCrNi and CoCrFeNi systems (E1-E3), but none of the cited evidence involves AlCrFeNiSi or even Al-containing HEAs, so the critical premise that these mechanisms and property improvements transfer to this specific composition is unsupported. The cited passages accurately describe L-PBF effects for the alloys they studied, but the generalization gap leaves most key premises without direct support for the target material.
premises: L-PBF rapid solidification and repeated remelting refine grains and create dislocation substructures in HEAs
L-PBF ultra-high cooling rates inhibit grain growth and elemental segregation
L-PBF can improve yield and ultimate strength of HEAs compared to conventionally processed alloys
Conventional casting of HEAs suffers from low solidification rate, element segregation, and rough microstructure
The cited evidence on CoCrNi/CoCrFeNi systems generalizes to the AlCrFeNiSi composition
